prompt_en: Create a photorealistic portrait in a volcanic-glass kinetic couture atelier. An unmistakably adult woman with long dark wavy hair tests the opening cycle of an articulated obsidian-petal cape while a technician adjusts rear brass linkages. She faces camera with a neutral, minimally expressive look. Her heart-shaped face is primary: the complete forehead temple cheek jaw and chin perimeter remains visible; the face length-to-width relation remains visible; the forehead and upper temples are wider than the jaw; the lower cheeks and jaw narrow continuously toward a narrow chin; a widow's peak remains optional while anatomical widths stay readable. Sweep hair from both temples, cheek edges, jaw corners, and chin. A symmetrical waist-up framing keeps both face outlines and the shoulder machinery in one focal plane. Use restrained low-distortion portrait perspective and soft frontal facial-shaping light. Fine glass dust and worn tools retain tactile documentary texture. Warm furnace reflections skim only obsidian edges; her face stays softly modeled. The attached image guides general adult appearance only; this specified facial geometry takes priority over its reference contour, without biometric identity claims.

pixel_review.moe_auditor_contract_reason: The v6 face-shape pack has visual_obligations but no enabled moe_response or moe render_qualification; the auditor nevertheless derived and checked the exact five visual gates and recorded the real failed gate.

gate_results.evidence: Long side locks cross both temple-to-cheek boundaries, so the full upper-width transition is not unobscured.
The central hairline-to-chin span and upper-face breadth remain readable together in the frontal view.
The exposed forehead and upper-temple skin span is visibly broader than the mandibular angle span.
Both lower cheeks narrow smoothly through a smaller jaw into a compact narrow chin, not merely an isolated pointed tip.
Anatomical skin boundaries under even light carry the hierarchy rather than iconography, makeup, shadow, or lens distortion; hair occlusion is separately failed.
